title: The Clock of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In 1938, Astrid Winterbourne, a half-Dutch, half-Japanese pearl diver's son indentured to the Van Doorn Trading Company in Nagasaki's harbor, keeps the company's ledger of divers, debts, and names. When the Imperial Army requisitions the harbor and declares the ledger's foreign signatories enemy aliens, Astrid discovers his childhood protector, the diver Oka-san, is among those to be detained and deported. Bound by a peacetime promise to keep her name off any list that would take her from the sea, he falsifies records, trades secrets with both occupiers and smugglers, and finally must choose between exposing himself as a fraud to save her or letting the ledger — and his own history — be erased. The book ends with Astrid surrendering the true ledger to a military tribunal to prove Oka-san's identity, losing his place at the company but gaining, at last, a name and a belonging of his own.
about_author: Ansel Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from treaty-port Asia. He writes historical fiction about the people whose names survive only in margins.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A day in the harbor: diving for pearls, mending nets, copying entries into the Van Doorn ledger by lamplight. He believes history belongs to capitals and newspapers, not to a boy who smells of brine. Emotional beat: quiet contentment built on willful blindness.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He learns the ledger's power when a clerk erases a dead diver's debt with one line. Oka-san, who taught him to hold his breath, makes him promise: whatever lists are made, keep her name tied to the sea. Emotional beat: an oath given lightly, meant forever.

chapters.title: Gunmetal Morning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Soldiers arrive; the harbor is requisitioned, warehouses sealed, the company's foreign partners declared enemy aliens. Mr. Van Doorn hands Astrid the ledger and vanishes into the crowd. Emotional beat: the world tilting from ordinary to occupied overnight.

chapters.title: The Requisitioned Town
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Sergeant Ito, a conscripted accountant ordered to audit the trading company's books. He notices discrepancies in the diver rolls but cannot yet read their meaning. Emotional beat: two men circling the same paper from opposite sides.

chapters.title: What the Army Wants With Paper
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Interrogated about missing signatures, he realizes the ledger can condemn or protect every name in it. He hides the original beneath the floor of the drying shed. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Oka-san's Boat
chapters.summary: Oka-san's POV (rare, lyrical). She dives one last time on her own grounds, remembering Astrid as a child floating beside her boat, weighing whether to flee the harbor alone. Emotional beat: love measured against self-preservation.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He sees the detention roster: Oka-san's name, marked for deportation as an enemy collaborator because of her late Dutch husband. The promise collides with the state. Emotional beat: dread made concrete in ink.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Sergeants
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He offers Ito 'corrected' copies in exchange for delays, learning the sergeant is no monster — just a man following orders he resents. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance across a uniform.

chapters.title: Smugglers' Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Desperate for exit papers, he approaches harbor smugglers who once bought his pearls. Their price: the ledger's shipping routes, which would betray other families. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Empty Berth
chapters.summary: Ito's POV. Ordered to expedite deportations, Ito finds a berth reserved under a false name and begins quietly investigating who has been altering the rolls. Emotional beat: duty pulling against doubt.

chapters.title: What Mother Never Said
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Visiting his mother's grave, he confronts his own split inheritance — Dutch father, Japanese mother — and why he let himself believe history skipped people like him. Emotional beat: grief becoming clarity.

chapters.title: A Night of Forged Ink
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He forges Oka-san's registration as a widow of a neutral national, using skills learned from Van Doorn's clerks. It works — almost. One seal is wrong. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into terror.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. A fellow clerk, resentful of Astrid's rise, reports irregularities. Ito is ordered to arrest whoever altered the rolls within three days. Emotional beat: the net closing.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Oka-san's POV. Detained in a holding warehouse, she watches other divers' names read aloud and erased. She refuses to give Astrid's name even when pressed. Emotional beat: dignity as defiance.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A countdown chapter: he tries bribery, forgery, flight — each door shutting. The smugglers demand the routes; Ito demands the truth. Emotional beat: desperation stripping away every easy option.

chapters.title: The Drying Shed
chapters.summary: Ito's POV. Ito finds the hidden original ledger and reads it through the night — debts, kindnesses, Oka-san's decades of rescues at sea. He understands what the promise means. Emotional beat: a soldier choosing conscience over orders, silently.

chapters.title: Tribunal at the Custom House
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. At Oka-san's deportation hearing, Astrid walks in with the original ledger and confesses everything — the forgeries, the thefts, the promise — offering himself in exchange for her name being struck. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest act left.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ito's POV. Ito testifies that the ledger proves Oka-san's rescues of Japanese sailors, arguing her loyalty better documented than most citizens'. Oka-san is released; Astrid is detained for forgery. Emotional beat: justice arriving lopsided, but arriving.

chapters.title: The Cell Below the Harbor
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In detention, he hears the tide through a grate and finds an unexpected peace — he acted, and history happened to him at last. Ito visits, bringing rice and word that charges may soften. Emotional beat: stillness after the storm.

chapters.title: Release Papers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Van Doorn reappears, buys Astrid's freedom with political favors, and offers him his old desk back — if he forgets the whole affair. Emotional beat: the old life offered back like a trap.

chapters.title: The Sea Keeps Its Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He refuses the desk, takes work mending boats, and dives again beside Oka-san, who gives him a new entry for her private book of names: his own, written properly at last. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not assigned.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Epilogue, 1946, Astrid's POV. War has passed over Nagasaki like weather; the harbor rebuilds. Astrid opens a small chandlery and keeps a new ledger — of debts forgiven, promises kept, names remembered. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance, survival as a price worth its cost.
